To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the age-related decrease in the GABAA/BZ receptor binding in the cerebellar cortex was not observed in the cerebellums of calorie restricted old (24-month old) rats.
calorie restriction prevents the age-associated decrease in the GABAA alpha2 subunit gene expression in the rat cerebellum.
the aging associated changes observed in GABAA receptor gene expression in the rat cerebellum are prevented by calorie restriction.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of dietary manipulations and aging on the expression of the GABAR alpha subunit mRNA in the rat cerebellum.
the effects of calorie restriction on the GABAA receptors in the aging cerebellum.
the molecular basis of age and diet related changes in the GABAA receptors in the brain.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
calorie restriction prevents the age related changes in the GABAA receptors.
the age-related changes in GABA receptor expression are retarded in calorie restricted rats.
the GABAA receptors in the cerebellar granule cells of aged rats are functionally altered, and that calorie restriction prevents these changes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
dietary restriction may prevent age-related changes in gene expression and may be an effective way of retarding the aging process.
the age and diet related changes in GABAergic neurotransmission may be mediated by a change in GABAA receptor stoichiometry.
calorie restriction retards the age associated changes in the gamma-aminobutryic acidA receptor gene expressions in rat cerebellar granule cell layer.
The main takeaway from our work is that
calorie restriction can retard the aging associated changes at the molecular level.
the beneficial effects of dietary restriction on aging can be explained at the level of gene regulation.
dietary manipulation may be used to prevent the age-related changes in GABAergic neurotransmission.
